 High tides: State govt steps up preparedness, monitors flood-prone areas 
 High tides: State govt steps up preparedness, monitors flood-prone areas
 Local 20 Nov 2026 • 10:33 PM MYT Media Selangor (EN) News and current issues, inclusive for all.
 SHAH ALAM, Nov 20 - Selangor is stepping up monitoring in flood-prone areas ahead of the high-tide phenomenon expected from Monday (November 23) to Friday (November 27).
 State executive councillor for disaster management Mohd Najwan Halimi said special attention is being paid to the possibility of heavy rain during this period, which could increase the risk of overflowing water.
 “If the high-tide phenomenon coincides with heavy rain during this period, we must be prepared because the risk of flooding will be very high. When it rains, the volume of overflowing water will increase,” he said.
 Monitoring is also being carried out through ongoing cooperation with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), including sharing the latest information on weather changes and anticipated risks.
 Previously, Menteri Besar Dato' Seri Amirudin Shari called for preparations in high-risk areas to be reviewed immediately, ahead of forecasts of more frequent rainfall during the high-tide phenomenon.
 As of this morning, 1,874 flood victims from 513 families were housed at 14 temporary relief centres across four districts in Selangor.
 In a related development, Najwan said flood mitigation projects are also being monitored to ensure efforts to reduce disaster risks proceed smoothly.
 “These measures are important, as some areas that had not previously experienced flooding are now also facing this risk. Nevertheless, completed mitigation and flood prevention projects have shown positive results, with flood risks reduced in several areas,” he said.
 Previously, the state government implemented 255 immediate flood mitigation projects across Selangor with an allocation of nearly RM70 million.
 Of these, 177 projects had been completed as of November 4, while the remaining 78 were in various stages of implementation.
 The projects include installing water pumps, clearing drainage systems, and repairing riverbanks.
